items.q: What is the ITIL definition of value?
o: The perceived benefits, usefulness and importance of something
The amount of money a consumer pays for a product or service
The functionality offered by a product or service to meet a particular need
Assurance that a product or service will meet agreed requirements
items.x: Value is the perceived benefits, usefulness and importance of something. It is subjective and co-created. Option C defines utility and option D defines warranty.

items.q: A finance director approves the annual budget for a new HR platform but will not use it or define its requirements. Which role is the finance director performing?
items.x: The sponsor is the role that authorizes the budget for service consumption. The customer defines requirements and takes responsibility for outcomes, and the user uses the service.

items.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
A [?] is a configuration of an organization's resources designed to offer value for a consumer.
items.x: A product is a configuration of an organization's resources designed to offer value for a consumer. A service is the means of enabling value co-creation, and a service offering is a formal description of one or more services for a target consumer group.

items.q: A sales team uses a new reporting service. Which of the following is an OUTCOME of using the service?
o: A weekly sales dashboard is generated
Report data is refreshed every night
A new report template is created
Sales managers make faster and better-informed pricing decisions
items.x: An outcome is a result for a stakeholder enabled by one or more outputs. The dashboard, data refresh and template are outputs, meaning deliverables of activities. Better decisions are the result the stakeholder achieves.

items.q: Which of the following describes the UTILITY of a video-conferencing service?
o: It is available 99.9% of the time during business hours
It allows users to share their screens and record meetings
It can be restored within two hours after a major failure
items.x: Utility is the functionality offered by a product or service to meet a particular need: what it does, or fitness for purpose. Availability, capacity and recoverability are aspects of warranty: fitness for use.

items.q: An employee receives a headset that becomes their personal property as part of an onboarding service offering. Which component of the service offering is this?
items.x: Goods are supplied with ownership transferred to the consumer, who then takes responsibility for their future use. Access to resources does not transfer ownership, and service actions are activities performed by the provider.

items.q: What is the term for the joint activities performed by a service provider and a service consumer to ensure continual value co-creation based on agreed and available service offerings?
items.x: Service relationship management covers the joint activities that keep value co-creation going. Service provision is what the provider does to provide services, and service consumption is what the consumer does to consume them.

items.q: A company moves its email to a cloud provider. Which of the following is a cost IMPOSED on the company by the new service?
o: The cost of replacing ageing email servers
The salary of a dedicated email server administrator
The cost of maintaining on-premises backup hardware
The cost of training staff to use the new email platform
items.x: Services remove some costs from the consumer and impose others. Training users on the new platform is an imposed cost. The other options are costs the cloud service removes.

items.q: Which is the ITIL definition of an incident?
o: A cause, or potential cause, of one or more problems
An unplanned interruption to a service or reduction in the quality of a service
Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service
A request from a user for an agreed service action
items.x: An incident is an unplanned interruption to a service or reduction in the quality of a service. Option C describes an event and option D a service request. A problem is the cause, or potential cause, of incidents, not of other problems.

items.q: What is a known error?
o: A problem that has been analysed and has not been resolved
An incident that has been resolved using a workaround
A defect found during testing before release
An error in a configuration record
items.x: A known error is a problem that has been analysed but not yet resolved. It is usually documented together with a workaround so that incidents can be resolved faster.

items.q: Which statement best describes user experience (UX)?
o: The number of incidents a user reports in a month
The technical performance of an application measured by monitoring tools
The terms and conditions a user accepts before using a service
The sum of functional and emotional interactions a user has with a product or service and its provider
items.x: Experience covers both functional and emotional aspects of the interactions with a product or service and its provider. Technical metrics alone do not capture it, which is why experience-focused measures are used alongside them.

items.q: In ITIL, sustainability is considered across which aspects?
items.x: Sustainability considers the environmental, social and economic impact of products and services, for example energy use, ethical supply chains and long-term economic viability.

items.q: Which dimension of product and service management includes formal organizational structures, culture, roles and responsibilities, and staffing and competencies?
items.x: The organizations and people dimension covers structures, culture, roles, responsibilities, competencies and leadership needed to create value.

items.q: A bank decides to use an external provider for security monitoring because it cannot recruit enough qualified analysts. Which factor influencing supplier strategy does this illustrate?
items.x: Resource scarcity, meaning a shortage of people or skills that the organization cannot easily fill, often leads organizations to obtain capabilities from partners and suppliers.

items.q: A new data protection law changes how customer data must be stored. Which category of external factors does this belong to?
items.x: Laws and regulations are Legal factors in the PESTLE model (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental). PESTLE factors influence all four dimensions.

items.q: In ITIL (Version 5), within which dimension is the ITIL AI Capability Model described?
items.x: The AI Capability Model is described within the information and technology dimension, which covers the information, knowledge and technologies needed to manage products and services.

items.q: Which list contains ONLY activities of the ITIL product and service lifecycle?
items.x: The eight lifecycle activities are Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support. Plan, Engage, Obtain/build and Improve belong to the ITIL 4 value chain, and option C lists ITIL v3 lifecycle stages.

items.q: A team evaluates whether to buy a SaaS solution, develop the capability in-house, or partner with a specialist firm to obtain a new service component. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Acquire is about obtaining the components needed, including technology, people and supplier capabilities, through buy, build or partner decisions. Build creates and tests the solution itself.

items.q: Which statement about the product and service lifecycle is CORRECT?
o: Activities must always be performed in the order Discover to Support
Each product can only be in one activity at a time across its whole life
Support is only performed after a product has been retired
Activities are interconnected and can be combined in different sequences, for example in value streams
items.x: The lifecycle is not a fixed sequence. Activities interconnect, can run in parallel and are combined into value streams. Different versions of a product can sit in different activities at the same time.

items.q: Users cannot access a customer portal. The team restores access, informs the users and records what was learned so that the product can be improved. Which lifecycle activity is mainly being performed?
items.x: Support helps users and restores normal operation when something goes wrong, and feeds what is learned back into the product. Transition moves new or changed products into the live environment.

items.q: Which guiding principle states that all activities conducted by the organization should link back, directly or indirectly, to value for itself, its customers and other stakeholders?
items.x: This is the essence of 'focus on value'. Applying it means knowing who the consumer is, how they use the service, and what value means to them, including their experience.

items.q: Before replacing its ticketing tool, a team carefully observes which existing workflows and reports already work well so that they can be reused. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: 'Start where you are' advises against building something new without considering what is already available to be leveraged. It also recommends observing the current state directly.

items.q: 'Comprehend the whole, but do something' is advice for applying which guiding principle?
items.x: 'Progress iteratively with feedback' warns against analysis paralysis. Understand the big picture, then deliver in small, manageable steps and use feedback to adjust.

items.q: A team displays all of its work on a shared Kanban board so that stakeholders can see bottlenecks and priorities. Which guiding principle does this MOST directly support?
items.x: Making work visible helps people understand what is being done, how work flows and where bottlenecks are, and so supports better decisions and collaboration.

items.q: Which guiding principle recognizes that no service, or element used to provide a service, stands alone?
items.x: 'Think and work holistically' requires working on the product or service as a whole, considering all four dimensions and how the parts interact, instead of optimizing parts in isolation.

items.q: A change request form contains 45 fields, but approvers only use 10 of them. Which guiding principle would MOST directly recommend reducing the form?
items.x: 'Keep it simple and practical' says that if a process, service, action or metric fails to provide value or produce a useful outcome, it should be eliminated. Use the minimum number of steps needed.

items.q: A manager wants to automate an approval workflow immediately. Several of its steps add no value. What does the 'optimize and automate' principle recommend?
o: Automate every step now and remove the unnecessary ones later
Simplify and optimize the workflow first, then automate it
Never automate approvals, because human judgement is always needed
Ask the tool vendor to decide which steps to automate
items.x: Optimize before you automate. Automating a wasteful process only produces waste faster. Define metrics to measure the effect of the optimization and automation.

items.q: Which activities are performed by a governing body?
items.x: Governance is carried out through evaluate (the organization, strategy and environment), direct (strategies and policies) and monitor (performance and conformance).

items.q: Which statement BEST describes governance?
o: The day-to-day planning and control of operational activities
The set of documented procedures used by support teams
The means by which an organization is directed and controlled
items.x: Governance is the means by which an organization is directed and controlled. Management plans and runs activities within the direction set by governance.

items.q: What is the FIRST step of the ITIL continual improvement model?
o: Where do we want to be?
items.x: The model starts with 'What is the vision?', which links the improvement to the organization's vision and objectives. It continues with where are we now, where do we want to be, how do we get there, take action, did we get there, and how do we keep the momentum going.

items.q: Which step of the continual improvement model involves performing a baseline assessment of the current state?
items.x: 'Where are we now?' establishes an objective baseline of current services, practices, capabilities and culture, so that progress can later be measured.

items.q: What is the purpose of a continual improvement register (CIR)?
o: To record all incidents and their resolutions
To store details of configuration items and their relationships
To track and manage improvement ideas from identification through to final action
To record approved changes and their implementation dates
items.x: A CIR is a structured record used to capture, prioritize, track and manage improvement ideas. An organization can have several CIRs, for example at team and organization level.

items.q: What is a management practice?
o: A set of interrelated activities that transform inputs into outputs
A documented procedure for one team
A software tool that automates workflows
A set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective
items.x: A practice is a set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective. It draws on all four dimensions. Option A defines a process, which is only one part of a practice.

items.q: What is the purpose of the incident management practice?
o: To minimize the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible
To reduce the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying their causes
To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests
To ensure that no incidents ever occur
items.x: Incident management restores normal service as quickly as possible to minimize impact. Identifying causes (B) is problem management, and capturing demand (C) is the service desk.

items.q: What are the inputs to the ITIL value system?
items.x: Opportunity (options to add value or improve) and demand (the need or desire for products and services) trigger activities in the value system. The value system's outcome is value.

items.q: Which of the following is a component of the ITIL value system?
items.x: The value system brings together the guiding principles, governance, the activities that turn demand into value, management practices and continual improvement. SLAs, a CMDB and PESTLE are not components of the value system.

items.q: What is a value stream?
o: A set of interrelated activities that transforms inputs into outputs within one team
A financial forecast of the value of a portfolio
A diagram showing the reporting lines of an organization
A series of steps an organization undertakes to create and deliver products and services to consumers
items.x: A value stream is the series of steps an organization undertakes to create and deliver products and services to consumers. It starts with demand and ends with value, and usually crosses team boundaries.

items.q: An organization's end-to-end hiring process provides new staff to internal teams so that they can deliver products to external customers. How would this value stream BEST be classified?
items.x: Core value streams deliver products and services directly to external consumers. Enabling value streams serve internal consumers so that the core value streams can work, and hiring is a typical example.

items.q: Which statement BEST describes generative AI?
o: AI that creates new content, such as text, images or code, based on patterns learned from data
AI that can only classify data into predefined categories
A rule-based script that runs the same steps every time
Any automated workflow that does not involve people
items.x: Generative AI produces new content (text, images, code, summaries) based on patterns learned from training data. Rule-based scripts and classification are other forms of automation or AI.

items.q: How do ITIL and DevOps relate to each other?
o: They are incompatible, so organizations must choose one
They are complementary: DevOps focuses on collaboration, automation and fast flow of changes, while ITIL provides broader guidance for managing products and services
DevOps replaces ITIL in organizations that use cloud services
ITIL is only for operations teams and DevOps is only for developers
items.x: ITIL is designed to work with approaches such as DevOps, Agile and Lean. DevOps practices like automation and continuous delivery fit within ITIL's broader value system and practices.
